extracted.subtask_description: Standards and failures relevant to producing and vetting investigative television news segments (especially those relying on documentary evidence and confidential sources). Covers authentication, source vetting, editorial oversight, and post-broadcast review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and accuracy (basic journalistic principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS News failed to follow basic journalistic principles; the American public has a right to count on CBS News for fairness and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic work must adhere to core principles of fairness and accuracy. The panel described the segment as "neither fair nor accurate" and urged reaffirmation of a commitment to the highest standards of journalism. Anti-patterns: publishing unverified or one-sided accounts that mislead the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to obtain clear authentication of the documents relied on in the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before broadcasting claims based on documents, obtain clear authentication (e.g., expert document examiners, corroborating evidence). The panel found serious defects including lack of clear authentication and noted that questions about the documents' authenticity (e.g., likely produced on a modern word processor) were raised almost immediately. Do not rely solely on the apparent truth of content as a substitute for authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough vetting of confidential sources' backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to investigate the controversial background of the source of the purported documents (retired Lt. Col. Bill Burkett).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and review all relevant background information about confidential sources so news judgments can be made. Anti-patterns include airing material without knowing a source's credibility, motives, or history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conflicts of interest / prevent appearance of political bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer Mary Mapes called Joe Lockhart (senior Kerry campaign official) before airing and offered to put Burkett in touch with him — called a "clear conflict of interest that created the appearance of political bias."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not take actions that create real or apparent conflicts (e.g., facilitating a source's contacts with political campaigns). Maintain independence from political actors; avoid conduct that could create the appearance of partisanship or influence timing/content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rush to air without sufficient investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guard segment was rushed on the air only three days after obtaining some of the documents, producing an inadequate vetting process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow adequate time for investigation and authentication before broadcasting, even under competitive pressure. Anti-patterns: compressing vetting into a short window (three days in this case) and thereby missing crucial checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify claimed confirmations and document what was said
rubrics_metrics.description: Mapes said Maj. Gen. Bobby Hodges 'confirmed' content when read to him over the phone, but Hodges denied doing so when interviewed by the panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on secondhand or informal oral confirmations; seek direct, documented corroboration. If relying on a verbal confirmation, record or obtain contemporaneous notes and follow up with written or independently verifiable evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rigid/blind defense; investigate when questions arise
rubrics_metrics.description: CBS News 'compounded the error by blindly defending the story' and made 'virtually no attempt' to determine whether raised questions had merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When credible questions or criticisms emerge, promptly re-evaluate the report, investigate the concerns, and, if necessary, correct the record. Anti-patterns: doubling down without reexamination, treating criticism as attack rather than as potentially valid checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow managerial directives and promptly review expert opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Order by CBS News President to review opinions of document examiners and confidential sources was not followed; had it been followed promptly, public defense would have been curtailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When senior management directs review (especially of external expert analyses), follow through quickly and document the review. Prompt compliance can prevent prolonged public defense of flawed reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insulate reporting from competitive pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'myopic zeal' to be first and competitive pressures contributed to producing a story that did not meet internal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster an atmosphere where competition does not prompt premature airing. Editorial decisions should prioritize accuracy over speed. Anti-patterns: prioritizing scoops at the expense of verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a senior Standards and Practices executive role
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to appoint a senior Standards and Practices Executive, reporting directly to the President of CBS News, to review investigative reporting, use of confidential sources and authentication of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a high-level, independent editorial oversight position to review sensitive investigative pieces and provide a confidential channel for staff to raise concerns without fear of reprisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require senior management access to confidential source identities and relevant background
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow senior management to know the names of confidential sources as well as all relevant background needed to make news judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Senior editors should have the necessary information about confidential sources (kept confidential internally) to assess credibility and make informed editorial decisions. This is for internal judgment, not public disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an independent team to review challenged reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint a separate team, led by someone not involved in the original reporting, to investigate any news report that is challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a report is contested, assign an independent review team (unconnected to the original reporting) to re-examine the evidence and the reporting process to ensure impartial assessment and restore credibility if errors are found.
